package_info.package_manager: malware-as-a-service (standalone binary, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: 2.3.0 (and earlier, as referenced by IOCs from May 2021)
package_info.why_malicious: Raccoon Stealer is a credential and cryptocurrency information stealer, distributed as a malware-as-a-service platform. It is explicitly designed to exfiltrate sensitive user data, evade detection, and facilitate cybercrime. The tool includes features for credential theft, anti-analysis, bot blocking, and reporting, all of which are malicious in intent and execution.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates installed browsers, extracts stored cookies and passwords, and sends this data to a command-and-control server, resulting in credential and session theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated extraction and exfiltration of browser credentials and cookies is a hallmark of infostealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software should never access and transmit all stored browser credentials/cookies without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise password managers may access browser data, but only with user authorization and never exfiltrate to unknown servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code locates and reads data from known cryptocurrency wallet files, then exfiltrates this information to a command-and-control server, enabling theft of cryptocurrency assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing and exfiltrating cryptocurrency wallet data is a direct attack on user financial assets.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications should not access or transmit wallet data without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities may access wallet files, but only with user permission and never transmit to unknown servers.
key_indicators: Network exfiltration of sensitive financial data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code monitors for multiple accesses from the same IP address or range, blocks these IPs, and hides the admin panel, thereby evading analysis and automated security scanning.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Blocking IPs based on access patterns is a common anti-analysis and anti-crawler technique in malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely implements such aggressive anti-analysis measures, especially in credential management tools.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Web applications may block abusive IPs, but not in the context of hiding C2 admin panels from researchers.
key_indicators: Automated IP blocking based on access patterns

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code detects IP addresses associated with crawlers or bots, blocks them, and reports these IPs to the C2 infrastructure, enhancing evasion and operational security.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Active detection and blocking of security researchers and crawlers is a clear sign of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not attempt to evade security monitoring in this manner.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some web services block known bots, but not in the context of malware C2 operations.

attack_chain.action: Initial infection and execution of the Raccoon Stealer binary on the victim's system.
Enumeration and extraction of browser credentials and cookies.
Enumeration and extraction of cryptocurrency wallet data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of wallet data to C2

attack_chain.action: Exfiltration of all collected data to command-and-control servers.
Detection and blocking of security researchers, crawlers, and automated analysis tools.

behavioral_signatures: Automated extraction of browser credentials and cookies
Access to known cryptocurrency wallet files
Network exfiltration of sensitive data to suspicious domains/IPs
Active detection and blocking of multiple accesses from the same IP
Reporting and blocking of crawler/bot IPs
file_indicators: Presence of Raccoon Stealer binary (hashes: e.g., 012e382049b88808e2d0b, c993ce24a57c99dd93d1, etc.)
Unusual access to browser credential stores and wallet files
network_indicators: Connections to telete[.]in, tttttt[.]me, telecut[.]in, tgraph[.]io, telegram[.]cat, telegram[.]services, tlgr[.]org, xn--r1a[.]click, xn--r1a[.]link, xn--r1a[.]live, xn--r1a[.]site, xn--r1a[.]website
HTTP/S requests to URLs such as hxxps://telete[.]in/jiocacossa, hxxps://tttttt[.]me/kokajakprozak, etc.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for processes accessing browser credential stores and cryptocurrency wallet files, especially if followed by outbound network connections to known Raccoon Stealer C2 domains or IPs. Look for binaries matching known Raccoon Stealer hashes. Detect anti-analysis behaviors such as blocking or reporting of security research IPs. Use network security tools to flag connections to suspicious Telegram-like domains and related infrastructure.
